title: A Phase 2 Study to Evaluate MAR002 for Acromegaly
official: A Phase 2, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multiple-Dose Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of MAR002 in Participants With Acromegaly (TROUGH-2)
summary: Main objective: To assess the safety and tolerability of multiple SC dose administrations of MAR002 and to assess the effect of MAR002 on serum IGF-1 levels in participants with acromegaly
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Willing to provide written informed consent and comply with study procedures as specified in this protocol and comply with study treatment.
2. Age 18 to 75 years (inclusive) at screening with active acromegaly confirmed by an endocrinologist specialized in the care of pituitary patients. At a minimum, there must be documentation of a pituitary tumor (e.g., imaging evidence of a pituitary tumor by magnetic resonance imaging [MRI]/computerized tomography [CT] or histopathologic evidence of pituitary adenoma following pituitary surgery) and an elevated IGF-1 in the past.
3. Participants receiving acromegaly medical therapy at screening (i.e., Group 2 and Group 3) may be enrolled if the regimen is considered stable by the Investigator and must agree to wash out acromegaly treatment
4. Average serum IGF-1 level of ≥ 1.3 × ULN defined as the mean of 2 measurements obtained ≥ 1 week apart during Screening. Note: for participants who do not require washout, the average should be calculated using measurements from SV1 and Screening Visit 2 (SV2). For participants who do require washout, the average should be calculated using measurements from the washout Visit and SV2.
5. Participants with hypothyroidism and adrenal insufficiency should have these hormone axes adequately replaced as judged by the Investigator.
6. Weight ≥ 50 kg at screening.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. History of hypersensitivity to monoclonal antibodies.
2. 18.  Pregnant or breastfeeding.
3. 19. Male participants who plan to donate sperm or who have a partner planning to become pregnant during the study and for 90 days after the last dose.
4. 10. Participants with diabetes treated with insulin for < 6 weeks prior to the study entry, or with an unstable insulin dose < 6 weeks prior to the study entry
5. 2. Participants who are biochemically controlled (defined as serum IGF-1 ≤ 1.0 × ULN) on the following regimens at baseline: a. SRL monotherapy b. DA monotherapy  c. SRL and DA combination therapy
6. 3. Participants who are on SRL, DA, and pegvisomant combination therapy (controlled or uncontrolled).
7. 4. Participation in any other investigational drug study and received the last dose of investigational drug within 60 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) of SV1.
8. 5. History of severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions.
9. 6. History of malignancy within 5 years prior to screening other than successfully treated basal or squamous cell carcinoma or localized cervical carcinoma. Any carcinoma in situ is allowed if appropriately treated within 2 years prior to screening. Participants with a history of malignancy ≥ 5 years prior to screening should be considered cured of their oncological disease.
10. 7. Pituitary surgery in the past 6 months prior to screening or any prior use of pituitary radiation therapy.
11. 8. Pituitary adenoma with concern for mass effect on the optic chiasm or other critical structures within the study period as per judgment of the Investigator.
12. 9. Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus, defined as having a hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) ≥ 9.0%.
13. 20. Significant illness, in the judgment of the Investigator, which has not resolved within 2 weeks prior to randomization.
14. 21. Any factor that may prevent the participant from safely undergoing an MRI, based on the standard clinical checklist, such as body habitus, claustrophobia, metallic implants or foreign objects, internal electronic devices, or permanent makeup/tattoos that are not confirmed to be MRI-safe
15. 22. Any condition that, in the opinion of the Investigator, prevents the participant from complying with study procedures or prevents the participant from completing the study or interferes with the interpretation of study results.
16. 11. Severe renal insufficiency (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR by Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration] < 30 mL/min/1.73 m 2 ) or significant liver disease (e.g., aspartate aminotransferase/alanine transaminase > 3 × ULN or total bilirubin > 2 × ULN (including Child-Pugh class B or C cirrhosis) prior to randomization.
17. 12. History or evidence of any of the following within the previous 12 months: myocardial infarction, cardiac surgery revascularization (coronary artery bypass grafting or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty), hospitalization for heart failure, or stroke or transient ischemic attack.
18. 13. Supine systolic blood pressure > 160 mmHg and/or supine diastolic blood pressure > 100 mmHg at SV1 or SV2 (if the initial measurement is out of range, may be repeated 2 more times after 15 minutes and exclusion will be based on the average of the 3 measurements).
19. 14.  Participants who are known to have uncontrolled HIV infection.
20. 15.  Participants with known active hepatitis A, B, or C. For hepatitis B, participants who are surface antigen negative and/or surface antibody positive can be considered for enrollment. For hepatitis C, participants with an undetectable viral load, defined as < 15 IU/mL, can be considered for enrollment.
21. 16. Blood donation of 450 mL or more within 3 months prior to Day 1.
22. 17. Participants not agreeing to follow specific contraception measures: a. Biological male participants not agreeing to use a condom (even if vasectomized) at the time of screening and for 90 days after the last dose of study treatment. b. Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) (defined in Section 6.2.3) not agreeing to use a combination of 1 highly effective method of contraception and 1 effective method of contraception (defined in Section 6.2.3) at least 28 days before the first dose of study treatment, continue during the study, and persist for 180 days after the participant’s last dose of study treatment, if applicable. Note:  WOCBP must have a negative serum pregnancy test at screening.
